Subject: Renewal planning + forecast (Solara)

Hi Jonas —

Hope you’re well. Our current Dedicated contract (SOL-2025-1543) is up for renewal June 30, 2027. We’re very happy with Redwood’s latency and the reserved pool behavior, but usage has grown faster than expected thanks to a new “assist” feature we launched in Q1.

High level:
- Q1 observed steady-state peak: ~1,800 QPS internal (text-generation), average prompt length ~320 tokens.
- Forecast: we expect peak QPS to rise to ~3,500 by Q4 2027 (new product lines + international traffic). Token-per-request estimate grows to ~420 tokens on average.
- SLA ask: would like a 99thpct p95 latency guard for our 2k token tail, and throughput guarantees for bursts up to +/-25% above peak for 15m windows.

Can you help us understand how many additional GPUs we should reserve for renewal, and whether a 24-month term vs 12-month would get us better pricing on the reserved pool? Attached is a simple forecast CSV. Procurement looped in for timing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

—Laura

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 17:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Solara renewal — need sizing, pricing options

Jonas / team —

We ran Solara’s forecast through the capacity model (assumptions below) and recommend the following committed pool adjustments and guardrails. Summary first, details after.

Summary recommendation:
- Baseline (current): 24xA100-equivalent GPUs committed; supports ~1.8k current peak with existing caching.
- Recommended committed pool for renewal: 44xA100-equivalent GPUs (net +20 GPUs) to cover forecasted steady-state peak of 3.5k QPS and provide ~25% burst headroom and KV/prefix cache hit smoothing.
- Autoscale buffer: allow on-demand bursting up to +40% for shortest windows (<=5m), with explicit contractual burst allowance of +25% for 15-minute windows. Anything beyond should gracefully fall back to next-best model variant (quantized 8-bit) where latency remains acceptable.
- Term recommendation: 24-month commitment yields ~12% per-GPU monthly discount vs 12-month, plus we can include one scheduled free capacity rebalance at month 12 if actual traffic deviates >15% from forecast.

Key assumptions used in model:
- Model family: mix of opt-6.7B (for shorter prompts) and opt-13B / gpt-style 30B variants for long-context product paths; CPU/KV cache hit assumptions: 60% prefix cache hit during steady-state, falls to 50% under burst.
- Average token generation cost scaled from 320->420 tokens: per-request inference time increases ~18% on average across model mix.
- GPU throughput: we used conservative per-GPU effective QPS of 80 for the long-context variants at 2k tokens tail; higher for shorter prompts. Effective blended per-GPU QPS = ~78.

Why +20 GPUs: 3,500 peak / 78 blended QPS/GPU = 44.8 -> round down to 44 and add 5% safety margin to protect against sequence-length variance and caching churn. That yields 44 committed and a pricing cushion to avoid immediate autoscale spend.

SLA/contract language to propose:
- Throughput guarantee: committed pool to sustain 3.5k steady-state QPS with contractual burst allowance of +25% for 15-minute windows. Redwood will provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns monthly.
- Latency guard: 95th percentile latency threshold for 2k tokens — target value TBD (match current observed p95 + allowance), we propose a joint runbook for incidents and automatic fallback to quantized variants after 10s of sustained overload.

Pricing stub (high level):
- 12-month term: $X,XXX per GPU/month (baseline).
- 24-month term: baseline * 0.88 (12% discount). Exact numbers hold at proposal stage; finance will finalize.

Open items / risks:
- Multi-region traffic: If >20% of traffic moves to EU/APAC, we recommend adding a 6–8 GPU regional buffer per additional region to maintain p95 for long-tail tokens.
- If Solara increases average tokens/request beyond 500, we should re-evaluate (could require +8 GPUs).

I’ll update the capacity_model_v2.xlsx with the exact calculation tab and send a customer-ready table.

—Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the forecast and patience while we ran the numbers. Attached is a short proposal (redwood-proposal-solara-2027.pdf) plus the capacity model tab we used. Key points:

- Recommended committed pool: 44 A100-equivalent GPUs (net +20), with contractual burst allowance of +25% for 15-minute windows.
- Autoscale policy: allow on-demand bursts to +40% for short windows (<=5m) but bill overage at standard on-demand rates. We’ll include a first-of-term monthly report showing token/latency breakdowns and trigger a mid-term rebalance if observed usage deviates >15% from the forecast.
- Term/price: 12-month baseline or 24-month with a 12% per-GPU monthly discount. If you opt for 24-month we’ll include one free capacity rebalance at month 12.
- Latency: we propose a p95 guard for 2k token tail; we’ll propose the exact target value in the final SOW after a joint benchmark (mktg + Solara test traffic).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm if the 44-GPU committed pool and burst terms align with internal approvals.
2) If yes, procurement can sign the attached amendment; target execution by May 10 to ensure capacity is reserved for the June 30 renewal.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-minute joint bench run to finalize the p95 target and replay your 1-week Q1 sample.

If you’d like, we can also do a shorter executive summary for your CFO/procurement that highlights cost delta for 12 vs 24 months.

Best regards,
Jonas
